papers.title_en: Harnessing SPAD Noise: Test-Time Gated Attention for Indoor Depth Estimation
papers.evidence: 单目深度估计，关注度量深度与零样本泛化
papers.tldr: 单目深度估计受尺度模糊、边缘渗色和零样本泛化差困扰；现有SPAD多模态方法多把噪声当有害伪影去噪或忽略。本文提出HSN，将SPAD原生噪声视为隐含环境先验，融合1D SPAD直方图与Gate Adapters，经三阶段优化生成通道门控注意力，在测试时动态调整编码器特征。在真实室内基准上取得域内SOTA metric depth，零样本泛化潜力更强，且可解释性显示噪声增强时注意力转向更深语义层。该轻量TTA框架无需密集3D模态或高计算开销。
papers.abstract_en: Monocular depth estimation (MDE) has emerged as a cost-effective alternative to hardware-dependent 3D sensing modalities, yet predicting precise metric depth remains a persistent challenge due to intrinsic scale ambiguity, edge bleeding, and limited zero-shot generalization in unseen environments. Recent multi-modal approaches incorporate 1D/3D Single-Photon Avalanche Diode (SPAD) data to resolve these ambiguities, but they mainly treat SPAD noise as a harmful artifact required for denoising or leave the noise ignored. In this paper, we present an essentially different insight: native SPAD noise is an informative prior that implicitly encodes deterministic environmental characteristics. Driven by this paradigm shift, we introduce a novel, lightweight Test-Time Gated Attention framework by Harnessing SPAD Noise, therefore dubbed HSN. Tailored for indoor scenarios, HSN leverages the synergistic combination of 1D SPAD histograms and Gate Adapters (GAs). Through three complementary optimization phases, it generates channel-wise gated attention vectors to dynamically adjust encoder feature maps at inference time, effectively resolving ambiguous scale and boundary challenges without the heavy computational overhead or dense 3D modalities that other TTA methods suffer from. Extensive experiments on challenging real-world indoor benchmarks show that HSN achieves state-of-the-art metric depth accuracy in in-domain settings, while exhibiting even greater potential under zero-shot generalization to unfamiliar environments. Furthermore, interpretability analysis reveals that the proposed gated attention mechanism adaptively shifts attention toward deeper semantic layers under intensifying SPAD noise. Code will be made publicly available.

papers.title_en: The Midas Touch for Metric Depth: Interpretable Metricization for Generalizable Depth Perception
papers.authors: Mengtan Zhang, Yu Ma, Shiqi Jiang, Yi Feng, Wei Ye, Xieyuanli Chen, Hanli Wang, Qijun Chen, Rui Fan
papers.evidence: 从相对深度基础模型恢复度量深度
papers.tldr: 单目相对深度估计泛化性虽因基础模型提升，但恢复准确度量深度仍受尺度模糊与局部尺度不一致困扰。现有显式仿射变换难适应空间变化关系，数据驱动补全又依赖稀疏观测分布。MTDv2提出混合框架：先以分段仿射变换显式度量化并保持几何结构，再通过可学习多路径细化传播度量观测。在16个数据集上，它跨多种稀疏观测与深度范式稳健恢复尺度，并适用于下游3D感知。
papers.abstract_en: Recent foundation models have drastically improved the generalization of monocular relative depth estimation, yet recovering accurate metric depth from their estimates for depth perception tasks remains challenging due to scale ambiguity and local metric-scale inconsistency. Existing approaches recover metric depth from sparse observations using either explicit global affine transformation algorithms or implicit data-driven depth completion networks. The former cannot accommodate spatially varying relative-to-metric relationships, while the latter are sensitive to the distribution of sparse observations and may not fully exploit generalizable relative depth priors. To simultaneously address these issues, this study extends our previous work MTD and proposes MTDv2, a hybrid metric depth perception framework that combines explicit depth metricization with data-driven metric depth refinement. The explicit depth metricization process performs segment-wise affine transformations to recover spatially varying metric scales while preserving the geometric structure of relative depth, followed by pixel-wise depth refinement that propagates metric observations along paths with minimal accumulated geometric variation. The data-driven depth refinement process subsequently extends the explicit single-path depth propagation to a learnable multi-path formulation while preserving its interpretability. Extensive experiments conducted on 16 public datasets demonstrate the robust and generalizable depth scale recovery capability of MTDv2 across diverse sources of sparse observations and different depth estimation paradigms, as well as its broad applicability to downstream 3D perception tasks. Code will be publicly available at https://mias.group/MTD upon publication.

papers.title_en: OpenDepth: Repurposing Image Editing Priors for Robust Open-World Monocular Depth Estimation
papers.authors: Mengke Zhang, Tianyi Yang, Xinzhuo Li, Anlong Ming
papers.evidence: 利用图像编辑先验实现鲁棒的开放世界单目深度估计
papers.tldr: 单目深度估计借助生成先验已取得SOTA，但基于T2I模型的方法在光照变化、恶劣天气等开放世界扰动下性能骤降，易产生结构幻觉。为此，OpenDepth将开放世界深度估计建模为多风格图像间的一致几何推理，复用I2I模型的结构保持编辑先验，并引入域内感知，通过DiT浅层特征对齐与RGB潜在重建任务解耦环境风格干扰。在标准及极端天气基准上，该方法刷新鲁棒零样本深度估计的SOTA，展现出优异的结构完整性与适应性。
papers.abstract_en: Recently, the integration of generative priors has revolutionized Monocular Depth Estimation (MDE), achieving state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance with remarkably high data efficiency. However, although methods based on Text-to-Image (T2I) models excel in general scenes, their efficacy degrades sharply when confronted with open-world environmental perturbations, such as illumination variations and adverse weather. Since T2I priors are optimized for semantic synthesis rather than preserving pixel-level structure, they struggle to decouple geometry from appearance under severe visual shifts, easily triggering structural hallucinations. Therefore, our core insight is to model open-world depth estimation as consistent geometric inference across multi-style images, fully leveraging the powerful structure-preserving editing priors of Image-to-Image (I2I) models. Based on this, we propose OpenDepth, a robust open-world MDE framework that introduces "Intra-Domain Awareness" -- the capability to map diverse stylistic inputs sharing identical geometry into a unified latent space. To achieve this, we first align shallow features within the Diffusion Transformer (DiT) to anchor degraded observations to unified geometric representations. Additionally, we introduce a joint RGB latent reconstruction task, requiring the model to recover clean RGB information from degraded inputs. This multi-stage strategy effectively decouples environmental style interference, compelling the model to focus strictly on underlying geometric recovery. Extensive evaluations show that OpenDepth sets new SOTA records for robust zero-shot depth estimation across standard and extreme weather benchmarks, demonstrating exceptional structural integrity and adaptability.

papers.title_en: UniMetric: Universal Metric Scale Recovery for Visual Geometry Foundation Models
papers.authors: Lei Yang, Yuner Zhang, Ziyang Liu, Ziying Song, Kai WU, Yiyang Gao, Jiangtao Su, Yiming Li
papers.evidence: 面向几何基础模型的免训练度量尺度恢复
papers.tldr: 视觉几何基础模型常能恢复场景结构与相机运动，却缺乏可靠度量尺度，而具身预训练需要物理尺度标注。UniMetric 无需额外传感器或任务监督，利用 VLM 提取常见物体高度先验，经语义-几何对齐转为尺度区间，再以凸优化全局求解统一尺度。在九种模型、MetricBench 十二个子集上，深度 Abs Rel、Chamfer 距离和轨迹误差分别降低 54.2%、83.8% 和 65.6%。该框架实现免训练通用尺度恢复，并发布代码与基准。
papers.abstract_en: Recent advances in multimodal foundation models, exemplified by GPT-6 Astra, raise the prospect of general-purpose embodied reasoning and planning. Using Internet videos for embodied pretraining calls for reliable physical-scale annotations. Yet visual geometry foundation models often recover scene structure and camera motion without reliable metric scale. We show that uncertain size priors of familiar objects can jointly constrain a reconstruction's shared scale. Building on this insight, we present UniMetric, a universal and training-free metric scale recovery framework for geometry foundation models, without additional sensors or task-specific metric supervision. Specifically, Metric Prior Acquisition elicits object height intervals from a vision-language model. Semantic-Geometric Alignment measures reconstructed object heights along the estimated support-surface normal in each frame and converts the priors into scale intervals. Global Scale Recovery reconciles these intervals through a convex objective, yielding a jointly feasible scale when they overlap and a unique compromise otherwise. The estimated sequence-level scale is applied uniformly to reconstructed points and camera translations. Controlled experiments with real VLM priors show that combining observations improves scale accuracy with exact relative object heights. To evaluate metric accuracy on GFM reconstructions without ground-truth scale alignment, we introduce MetricBench, covering twelve embodied, driving, and roadside subsets with sensor-derived ground truth. Across nine geometry foundation models, UniMetric reduces mean depth Abs Rel, reconstruction Chamfer distance, and trajectory error by 54.2%, 83.8%, and 65.6%, respectively, improving every model on all three tasks at the suite level. We release the UniMetric code and MetricBench data.

papers.title_en: Dense Endoluminal Mapping and Localisation from Monocular Bronchoscopy
papers.authors: Salvatore Esposito, Matias Mattamala, Daniel Rebain, Liang Zhao, Kev Dhaliwal, Mohsen Khadem, Subramanian Ramamoorthy
papers.evidence: 以Depth Anything 3为主干输出度量逐像素深度
papers.tldr: 支气管镜定位通常依赖电磁追踪和术前CT，额外设备与配准流程限制了临床应用。本文提出仅用单目RGB视频的SLAM系统，用微调后的Depth Anything 3提供度量深度作为唯一尺度来源，用DINOv3特征经交叉注意力匹配器在黏膜上获取亚像素对应。两者与投影ICP对自身重建的稠密约束共同进入因子图。在六条患者CT渲染气道上取得26.1毫米平均轨迹误差与77.5%表面F-score，并可处理离体标本。
papers.abstract_en: Bronchoscopy inserts a camera through the airways to diagnose endoluminal disease. Locating the camera along the airway usually requires additional equipment, such as an electromagnetic tracker and a preoperative CT scan. In this paper, we investigate the use of the monocular camera stream to localise the bronchoscope without requiring additional sensing. We introduce a monocular SLAM system that localises the tip of a bronchoscope and reconstructs the airway surface around it from RGB video alone. A Depth Anything 3 backbone, fine-tuned on over a million photorealistic airway renderings, returns metric per-pixel depth and is the system's only source of scale. DINOv3 features routed through a custom cross-attention matcher supply sub-pixel correspondences on mucosa where classical descriptors fail. Both enter a factor graph alongside a dense constraint from projective iterative closest point (ICP) registration against the system's own running reconstruction, so surface evidence stabilises the directions the visual factors leave weakly observable. On six airways rendered from patient CT scans, the system reaches 26.1 mm mean absolute trajectory error and 77.5% mean surface F-score. Its mean surface accuracy exceeds that of five recent monocular SLAM and feed-forward baselines. MASt3R-SLAM, which fits a free scale to the ground truth, has a lower mean trajectory error (22.0 mm). ORB-SLAM3 completes only two of the six airways, whereas our system completes all six and also reconstructs two ex vivo specimens.
